title: The Math Error That Cost Intel Millions #Shorts

hook.narration: In nineteen ninety-four, a tiny math error cost Intel hundreds of millions of dollars.

visuals.prompt: A glowing computer processor chip cracked down the middle on a dark workbench, 1990s

scenes.narration: A professor, Thomas Nicely, noticed that Pentium chips sometimes gave wrong answers to certain division problems.

visuals.prompt: A 1990s mathematics professor at a beige desktop PC comparing two printouts of numbers, puzzled
A whiteboard filled with long division and one number circled

scenes.narration: Intel said the error was rare and most users would never see it.

visuals.prompt: A 1990s corporate press conference with a spokesperson at a podium and camera flashes

scenes.narration: Customers and the press weren't convinced, and IBM halted shipments of its Pentium computers.

visuals.prompt: Frustrated 1990s customers holding beige computers and newspaper headlines about a chip flaw
A warehouse of boxed beige IBM computers stacked and shipment stopped, dim light

scenes.narration: Finally, Intel offered to replace every affected chip, at a cost of about four hundred seventy-five million dollars.

visuals.prompt: A technician replacing a processor chip in a beige 1990s PC under bright light

description: The Pentium FDIV bug of 1994 started with a professor's odd result and ended with a huge recall. #Shorts #History #Tech

thumbnail.prompt: A cracked glowing processor chip on a dark circuit board, 1990s beige PC in background
